references.text: Judah tells Tamar to wait for his youngest son Shelah, as a continuation of the levirate duty he imposed on Onan in verse 8.
The Mosaic law provision regarding levirate marriage, which directly relates to Judah's instructions to Onan to raise up offspring for his brother.
Boaz takes on the levirate duty toward Ruth, an important example of the same practice that Judah imposes on Onan.
Naomi refers to the levirate custom when she explains that she has no more sons who can marry her daughters-in-law.
Jesus refers to levirate marriage in a discussion with the Sadducees, showing that this practice from Genesis 38:8 was known and practiced in New Testament times.

Clear contrast: Both verses involve Tamar and a brother sending word to 'go' to him, but while Genesis 38 deals with the holy duty to raise up offspring, 2 Samuel 13 is about abuse and the breaking of that same family structure.
